content.title: Wednesday Evening Briefing
content.lead: This evening's most important news: Investigation successful after attempted attack on Leipzig Airport ++ Suspected attack on Cologne substation ++ What the drama surrounding Harry and Meghan reveals about the British
content.author: Marcel Urech

content.text: You can only read this in the NZZ: The CDU and SPD are in decline, while the AfD and Left Party are gaining ground. Parties from the «fringe» are finding more support than those from the «center.» This complicates the formation of homogeneous coalitions, extremism researcher Eckhard Jesse wrote in the run-up to the state elections in Saxony-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, and Berlin. To the guest commentary

content.title: Attempted attack on Leipzig Airport: Two suspects with Russian connections identified

content.text: What happened: Investigators from the Federal Criminal Police Office apparently identified two suspects in the attempted attack on Leipzig Airport. The logistics provider and instructor for the attack was a Russian-born man with a Latvian passport, NDR, WDR, and the «Süddeutsche Zeitung» reported. He had connections to the Russian intelligence service, the outlets said. The second suspect was a Belarusian, they added. He also possessed a Russian passport and had previously attracted attention for criminal offenses in the Baltics, the outlets said. To the latest developments

How the EU is reacting: EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said that the incident in Leipzig represented a new escalation on European soil. She added that it would further strengthen the EU's resolve to increase pressure on Russia. To the report

How Russia is reacting: The Kremlin categorically denies responsibility for the incident in Leipzig and portrays the German accusations as an act of desperation by a weak government. The sanctions imposed by Germany were a «serious mistake,» Vladimir Putin said. Moscow has already announced countermeasures. To the report

Background: On Aug. 4, security personnel at Leipzig Airport discovered a drone rigged with explosives and a detonator. More drones were found later. The Office of the Attorney General considers the incident a serious attack on Germany's transport and logistics infrastructure. The German government holds the Russian intelligence service responsible for it.

content.title: Substation disturbance near Cologne: Chief public prosecutor's «very strong indication» of intentional crime

content.text: What happened: Following the disturbance at a substation near Cologne, investigators found six launch devices in a cornfield. It was to be assumed that they were built to guide a wire over the power lines using pyrotechnical objects, the Senior Criminal Director said. From the perspective of the investigating chief public prosecutor, the discovered devices were a «very strong indication of an intentional criminal offense.» To the report

Situation in Brandenburg: On Tuesday morning, unknown individuals attempted to trigger short circuits on high-voltage lines at a substation in Brandenburg. Authorities are now investigating on suspicion of forming a terrorist organization. To the report

Background: The incidents in Brandenburg and North Rhine-Westphalia highlight how difficult it is to secure critical infrastructure across the board. Attacks on it are likely to increase in the future. To the analysis
Trump's increased pressure over the Strait of Hormuz: For the first time, the U.S. attacked Iranian oil tankers. Tehran, in turn, targeted American military bases in the Middle East. To the report
Nestlé's billion-dollar loss on vitamin brand sales: The world's largest food company once pursued ambitious plans in the health business. Now CEO Philipp Navratil is scaling them back. To the report

After flash flood in Nepal, death toll over 1000: Police in Kathmandu now report 1127 deaths in Nepal. China had previously reported 16 victims on the Tibetan side. The death toll is likely to rise further. 4600 people are still missing. To the latest developments

Suspected shooting rampage in Aarau incident: The Swiss suspect fired an assault rifle over 40 times into the crowd at a rave on Sunday morning and fled in a vehicle. The 43-year-old is reportedly mentally ill. To the report

image.altText: US President Donald Trump and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni shake hands as they pose for a photo, at a world leaders' summit on ending the Gaza war, amid a US-brokered prisoner-hostage swap and ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas, in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, October 13, 2025. Yoan Valat/Pool via REUTERS

content.text: Transatlantic Alliance: The alliance between the Maga movement and European right-wing populists is in crisis. Europe's nationalists have distanced themselves from U.S. President Donald Trump, even though their view of the continent aligns with his. Economic and geopolitical rifts have opened up that are insurmountable for the foreseeable future. To the background

Xi Jinping in Egypt: China's leader spends only two weeks a year abroad. Now he is visiting Egyptian President Abdelfatah al-Sisi. Why? Beijing is investing billions in the country, thereby securing influence over one of the most important trade routes. To the background

image.author: Hollie Adams / Reuters
image.altText: FILE PHOTO: Britain's Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, disembark after sailing on Sydney Harbor with veterans from the Invictus Australia community, in Sydney, Australia, April 17, 2026. REUTERS/Hollie Adams/File Photo

content.text: Harry and Meghan: King Charles's youngest son and his wife have returned to England from the U.S. The tabloids are reacting almost hysterically. The prince's behavior is often contradictory – but so is that of the media and the public. To the background

Possible AfD electoral victory: Ahead of the election in Saxony-Anhalt, FDP leader Wolfgang Kubicki brings up the instrument of federal coercion against a possible AfD state government – i.e., coercive measures in case of legal violations. But when would such measures even be permitted? To the background

🎧 Listen: Beijing is trying by all means to destabilize Taiwan without a single shot being fired. Sinologist and intelligence expert Jürgen Kremb describes in «NZZ Geopolitik» how China infiltrates the island with cyberattacks, disinformation, and espionage. To the podcast

📱 Erleben: Digital communication technologies have revolutionized the way we interact. What used to be formal and slow is now casual and fast. But who controls the networks and content? And what does it mean to hand a toddler an iPad? Discuss online this Thursday at the «NZZ Podium.» Register here
I wish you a pleasant evening.
Marcel Urech
The briefing is published on weekdays at 6 AM and 5 PM. On Saturdays, there is a weekend edition at 7 AM.
